misconceptions.description: Assuming evidence that a tool worked in one study or classroom transfers to any other setting regardless of context variables
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts a tool on study evidence without checking whether the study's context matches their own
misconceptions.feedback: Compare the context variables. Class size, device ratio, and language profile govern transfer; evidence from a different setting may not carry over.

misconceptions.description: Describing classroom context with vague labels instead of the decision-relevant variables
misconceptions.trigger: learner characterizes the room as 'a normal class' with no specific variables
misconceptions.feedback: Replace the label with decision-relevant variables: class size, device ratio, multilingual proportion, accommodations, and connectivity.

misconceptions.description: Accepting an AI tool recommendation that was made without knowing the classroom's context variables
misconceptions.trigger: learner takes a context-free AI recommendation as a fit judgment for their specific room
misconceptions.feedback: Feed the AI your actual context variables and ask it where the tool might fail for your room, then judge the fit yourself.

misconceptions.description: Generalizing a tool as good or bad from one section's outcome without diagnosing which context variable changed
misconceptions.trigger: learner declares a tool reliable or unreliable based on differing results across periods
misconceptions.feedback: Differing results across sections usually mean differing context variables. Identify which variable changed before generalizing about the tool.
